newsitem.title: JAPAN: S.AFRICA CUTS SILICO-MANGANESE EXPORTS TO JAPAN.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA CUTS SILICO-MANGANESE EXPORTS TO JAPAN.

text.p: South Africa has reduced exports of silico-manganese to Japan after the domestic Japanese price was depressed by a flow of cheaper shipments of Chinese origin, Japanese traders said on Monday.
"South Africa has been more keen to export the metal to the U.S. and Europe, as market prices there are much more attractive than those in Japan," one trader at a major trading house said.

The traders said imports of silico-manganese from South Africa's Samancor Ltd for the July-to-September period are expected to be around 3,000 tonnes per month, about one-third of the volume purchased in the same period a year earlier.

The prices quoted from the ferro-alloy giant in South Africa to Japanese customers for the July-to-September period were around $580 per tonne, including freight and insurance, compared with a price in the United States of around $660 to $670.
To compensate for the decline in South African supplies, Japan is expected to increase its imports from China.
"China is boosting exports of the metal to Japan partly because Chinese-origin product is likely to be subject to anti-dumping duties in the European market," another trading house trader said.
Chinese-origin silico-manganese was quoted in the Japanese market around $560 to $570.
Japan's imports of the metal, used mostly in steel making, amounted to 113,347 tonnes in the first six months of this year, according to the Japan Ferroalloy Association.
Of these, the main suppliers were China, Ukraine and South Africa.
